title: Why Dave disbanded the quartet and Paul Desmond's lifestyle
summary: Chris explains Dave wanted to stop touring and write orchestral and choral works, while Desmond liked his easy lifestyle and resisted.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well I want to back up and say one thing to your earlier question about Dave and the break-up of the group. Like for me, I wasn’t super on top of it because at that point I was going to Interlochen Arts Academy. So I knew it was going to happen, and it was predicted, but to give you some insights on that I mean I think really what drove that decision was Dave relentlessly being on tour for, you know, twenty years or something. And the next thing that he really wanted to do was devote himself to writing big orchestral pieces and choral pieces. And you know he gave everyone in the group like a warning of at least a year, maybe a year and a half, maybe two years. And they sort of said, “You’re not really going to disband our group,” you know, the most successful group. And if you’re Paul Desmond, you know Paul had it easy. He was a fantastic player and he could just show up and play beautifully. And Dave and Iola were doing all the work. And in between he could go to Bradley’s or Elaine’s and, you know, do his happy drinking and hanging out.
They could drag him on to the next plane to the next gig.
And I don’t mean he was a raging alcoholic but he just had a lifestyle.
He wouldn’t have traded it for anything.
Right. He was like. “Oh my God if you break up the group what am I going to do with my lifestyle?”
I’ll have to go to work.
